It is an earlier Eisenhower letter issued only twelve days before the child, uses the same Section 206 board-report-to-Section 208 injunction sequence, and closely matches the child’s distinctive concluding formulation concerning removal of a peril, resumption of interstate and foreign commerce, petitioning a federal district court, enjoining continuation of the strike, and seeking other necessary or appropriate relief. C12 and C01 are also strong precedents, but C15 is temporally closest and has the greatest literal and structural correspondence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"On October 9, 1959, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute","parent_excerpt":"On October 6, 1959, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in labor disputes","explanation":"The letters open with the same statutory authority, prior-directive reference, and Board of Inquiry machinery, adapted to different industries."},{"child_excerpt":"This morning, October 19, 1959, I received the Board's written report in the matter. A copy of that report is attached.","parent_excerpt":"On October 7, 1959, I received the Board's written report in the matter. I understand you have a copy of that report.","explanation":"Both proceed from creation of the inquiry board to receipt of its written report before making the statutory finding."},{"child_excerpt":"In my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade, commerce, and transportation among the several States and with foreign nations ... which strike will, if permitted to continue, imperil the national health and safety.","parent_excerpt":"In my opinion these unresolved labor disputes have resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and with foreign nations, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety","explanation":"The statutory finding is expressed through substantially identical syntax and vocabulary."},{"child_excerpt":"Therefore, in order to remove a peril to the national health and safety and to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, and transportation among the several States and with foreign nations ... I direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","parent_excerpt":"Therefore, in order to remove a peril to the national health and safety and to secure a resumption of trade, commerce, transportation, transmission or communication among the several States and with foreign nations, I direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any District Court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","explanation":"This is an extensive near-verbatim match in the operative direction and strongly indicates reuse of C15 as a drafting template."}]}
